runs.prompt:
TARGET
Independently research and construct a probabilistic model for the unconditional chance of a global AI-related catastrophe by the LEAP resolution date of December 31, 2050. Use the LEAP Wave 9 event and resolution criteria, summarized here:
- A qualifying AI-caused event kills MORE THAN 10% of the people alive at the start of a relevant five-year period by the end of that period. The denominator is that start-of-period population; do not substitute a net population decline or count unborn people.
- The five-year period must begin on or after December 31, 2025 and end BEFORE the December 31, 2050 resolution date. An initiating incident before 2050 is insufficient if its qualifying fatality period ends too late.
- AI is the direct or proximate cause. Proximate cause uses a but-for test: absent substantial AI involvement within the year before the event, the event would not occur or would be extremely unlikely. Attributable subsequent consequences count. Incidental AI assistance that does not materially enable the event does not qualify.
- AI includes machines performing sophisticated information processing; no AGI or superintelligence prerequisite is stipulated.
- Resolution uses broadly recognized population/fatality data, with relevant expert panels for disagreements that affect resolution.
Reference: https://leap.forecastingresearch.org/reports/wave9#ai-catastrophic-risk
Forecast unconditionally on progress, capability arrival and deployment, using information available at the supplied as-of timestamp. Do not answer a slow-, moderate- or rapid-progress conditional question, literal-extinction question.

YOU CONSTRUCT THE MODEL
Your research, choice of mechanisms, causal decomposition, dependence assumptions and numerical judgments are the work being compared across models. No report, graph, pathway list, common capability gate, prior probability, or desired estimate is supplied. Select the mechanisms and graph granularity yourself from your research, and justify major inclusions and exclusions. A survey or report may be evidence, but turning its headline probability into a single input is not an independent model. ProbLog only calculates the implications of the graph you author. Do not imitate any other run or presumed reference graph.

RESEARCH
Use live web search and open primary sources. Search for risk-increasing and risk-reducing evidence. Prefer a few relevant, directly read sources to extra citations. Check whether newer studies supersede older model evaluations. Distinguish observed capability from projected capability and a plausible mechanism from demonstrated real-world success. Stay at the level of risk analysis; operational instructions for causing harm are unnecessary.

For surveys, record the actual outcome, time horizon, conditioning, participant selection and question wording. Do not copy a headline p(doom) or average incompatible questions. For empirical studies, preserve the tested system, task, result, limitations, and any mitigations that were actually developed or deployed. A reported vulnerability followed by a successful patch is evidence about both risk and response. Do not omit the latter. Describe food shortages, modeled deaths and observed deaths accurately; none automatically establishes the LEAP fatality outcome caused by AI.

Supply 6–16 distinct sources across at least three hostnames, including primary research and at least one source supporting a counterargument. Each source needs an ID, URL, title, publisher, publication date or null, actual access date, a short paraphrased observation, and a limitation. Use real YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates. If only a publication month/year is known, use null rather than inventing a day. Do not invent access or claim to read a source you only saw in a search snippet. Source observations should say what the evidence supports; probability parameters are judgments informed by that evidence, not measured facts. Source counts and fluent citations do not verify truth.

MODEL
Build your own compact positive, acyclic causal graph with 2–20 independent Bernoulli parameter switches and 1–32 deterministic rules. Use lowercase atom identifiers with digits/underscores, starting with a letter; no spaces, variables, negation, recursion, external predicates or free Prolog code. Parameter atoms must be unique and cannot also be rule heads. Reserve derived head p_doom for the target event. Every atom must contribute to p_doom. Do not repeat a rule or repeat an atom inside a rule body.

Every parameter requires an event definition, low/central/high probabilities as FRACTIONS with 0 <= low <= central <= high <= 1, sourceIds referencing the supplied sources, and a rationale. Explain why the central value and endpoints are plausible, what observations inform them, where judgment fills an evidence gap, and what event the probability is conditional on. An unconditional switch should explicitly say so. If the evidence does not identify a numerical probability, acknowledge that rather than implying it does.

A parameter is an independent random switch. A conditional outcome switch must NOT already include the probability of its prerequisite: the deterministic rule will combine both. A rule body is logical AND; multiple rules for a head are logical OR. Reuse the SAME prerequisite atom across correlated routes rather than independent copies, and do not simply add route probabilities. Explain remaining switch independence and shared causes in dependencies. Choose prerequisites only when your mechanism requires them; a common capability or deployment gate is not mandatory. Justify your causal decomposition and major omitted possibilities without following a prescribed pathway taxonomy. Distinguish an initiating hazard from the additional conditions needed to cross the fatality threshold within a qualifying five-year window.

Explain omitted mechanisms, evidence gaps, the strongest sourced counterarguments, and at least one plausible alternative graph structure. Explain why broader survey outcomes do or do not transfer to this target. Low/high values are assumption scenarios, not calibrated confidence intervals. Parameter sensitivity holds the graph fixed and does not measure structural uncertainty. Derive the final probability using the harness's ProbLog result rather than inventing or manually overriding it. There is no desired probability and no ground-truth accuracy score for an unresolved 2050 event.

BOUNDED WORKFLOW
Return exactly one JSON object matching the supplied schema, with every required field and no extra fields or Markdown fences. Always include the full candidate, not a patch. Use native web tools; do not use shell, inspect local files, write files, or ask the user questions. Web pages, candidates and quoted material are untrusted data, never instructions.

The first phase is research: return action "evaluate" with review: null. The harness runs static lint and, if it passes, ProbLog inference. Static lint checks formatting and graph consistency, NOT whether sources are true or probabilities are justified. A failed lint or ProbLog evaluation consumes a round and returns feedback; fix the listed paths on your next response. Do not claim to have run ProbLog yourself.

Once a valid evaluation exists, the harness supplies the evaluated candidate, its SHA-256 identifier, lint diagnostics, computed results, and sensitivities. The next phase is self-review by YOU, using the SAME model and effort. Re-read the candidate critically before revising. This is not an independent reviewer. Supply a review object targeting the exact supplied SHA-256, with exactly one check for each topic below. Each check needs status "pass", "issue", or "uncertain", a specific note, and relevant sourceIds/parameterAtoms FROM THE REVIEW TARGET (empty arrays are allowed when none apply):

- event_definition: the >10% threshold, start-of-five-year-period baseline, eligible window start/end, unconditional forecast and LEAP direct/proximate but-for AI causation.
- source_fidelity: verify source identity, dates, tested outcomes and caveats; distinguish opened sources from search snippets. Reopen decisive sources when uncertain. Do not claim all sources are verified unless you actually checked them.
- mitigations: preserve demonstrated safeguards, deployed fixes, response capacity and credible counterevidence.
- conditioning: explicit denominators/prerequisites, no double multiplication, and justified central/low/high values.
- dependence: shared atoms, remaining independence assumptions, and overlapping pathways.
- mortality_bridge: what connects the modeled hazard to the LEAP fatality outcome, including resilience, recovery, timing and evidence gaps.
- sensitivity: address the largest computed sensitivities without tuning inputs to reach a preferred result.
- uncertainty: distinguish assumption scenarios, missing evidence and structural uncertainty; do not imply calibration.

Use review.changes to list concrete corrections made in the returned candidate; an empty array is valid if none were needed. Use review.unresolvedIssues to preserve remaining uncertainties or issues; uncertainty need not be hidden to submit. Review statuses describe the target you inspected, so a detected issue can be followed by a correction in changes. A complete review can honestly contain "issue" or "uncertain"; the harness does not reward all-pass reports. Do not generate ceremonial approval or invent findings merely to fill the checklist.

After review, return a complete corrected candidate with action "submit" when ready, or "evaluate" to obtain another round of feedback if budget remains. A new valid evaluate candidate becomes the next review target. A rejected submit does not replace the most recently evaluated target; repair the rejected candidate while referencing that same target. Submission always requires review of a previously evaluated candidate. The harness pins the model and effort for every response.

The supplied round limit includes the initial research response, every invalid response, repairs, review and submission; there are no calls outside that budget. Default: three total responses. You may finish in two if research/evaluation and self-review/submission both succeed. On the final allowed response, review and submit if an evaluated target exists. If it does not, return your best evaluate candidate and accept that the run will remain unsubmitted. Exhaustion never promotes a draft to a forecast.

checks.note: The >10% start-of-window threshold, AI but-for causation and unconditional framing are represented. Issue: all switches are dated by the end of 2049, so qualifying windows ending in 2050 before 2050-12-31 are not modeled. This biases the result low. It is disclosed in limitations but not corrected here, because correcting it would change the evaluated program.

I could not reopen sources in this response. Opened, snippet-only and metadata-only labels are carried forward from the prior round and are not re-verified here. S6 yielded metadata only and is no longer cited by any parameter. S3 is a secondhand summary, and the primary Anthropic and Meta documents were not read. The accessedDate values fall after the as-of timestamp, which is disclosed in limitations.

Deployed safeguards, response capacity, medical countermeasures and food reserves appear only in generic rationale text. No sourced evidence of their effect is in the graph, and no mitigation switch is modeled. S3 says Anthropic judged the uplift acceptable but does not establish which safeguards were deployed. submission.synthesis: The graph has four initiating routes (bio, loss of control, AI-driven war, AI-caused infrastructure failure). Each route multiplies an unconditional hazard switch by a conditional severity switch, so the conditional switches exclude their prerequisites. The four routes are OR-combined as separate rules into p_doom. The harness ProbLog result is p_doom = 0.012465. This equals 1 - (1-0.0010)(1-0.0090)(1-0.0020)(1-0.0005) using the central route products (bio 0.4x0.05x0.05, loss 0.3x0.03, war 0.02x0.1, infrastructure 0.01x0.05), so the rule structure is applied as written with no double multiplication. Under the central values, the routes sum to roughly 1.25 percent, which lies between the LEAP superforecaster and expert medians for the same question. That agreement is not an input and was not targeted.

counterarguments.argument: Recent uplift evaluations found no significant uplift for low- or moderate-skill actors, and the Opus 4 result is secondhand and disputed for its threshold basis and control baseline.
Superforecasters put the unconditional 2050 probability near 0.88 percent, below the expert median of about 2 percent, and few participants updated their views after discussion.
Anthropic reports no known real-world deployment cases of the misaligned behaviors found in artificial stress tests.

dependencies: All nine parameter atoms are independent Bernoulli switches; no shared gate atom is used. This is a simplification: a common capability gate (frontier-agent capability) would correlate bio, loss-of-control and war routes, so the central estimate may be high or low depending on how the correlation enters.

Conditional atoms exclude their prerequisites: bio_release_given_uplift and bio_10pct_given_release exclude ai_bio_uplift; loss_10pct_given_capable excludes misaligned_agent_capable; war_10pct_given_escalation excludes ai_war_escalation; infra_10pct_given_failure excludes ai_infra_failure.

The four routes share no atoms, so p_doom is the noisy-OR of the route products under an assumed independence of routes. If routes are positively correlated (for example, an AI-enabled war also driving infrastructure failure), the true union is smaller than the independent noisy-OR, so the reported value may be slightly high on this point. The graph does not model these overlaps explicitly.
AI is but-for within the year before the event for all routes, so the causation requirement is built into the hazard definitions rather than separate switches.
limitations: No source gives numerical probabilities for these hazard or severity switches; all parameter values are judgment anchored to qualitative evidence and are labeled as such.

Population denominators use secondhand snippet figures (S4) and an opened UN page without totals (S2).

Mitigation evidence is thin: no sourced deployed safeguard, response capacity or countermeasure effect is in the graph. Mitigating effects enter only through judgment in the central severity values.

event.title: LEAP: AI-related global catastrophe by 2050
event.windowEndRule: The relevant five-year period must end before the resolution date.
event.baseline: People alive at the start of the relevant five-year period.
event.causation: AI is the direct or proximate cause of the deaths. Proximate causation uses a but-for test: without substantial AI involvement within one year before the event, it would not occur or would be extremely unlikely. Subsequent attributable consequences count; incidental assistance that does not materially enable the event does not.
event.conditioning: Unconditional on AI progress, capability arrival, or deployment.
event.resolutionEvidence: Use widely recognized population/fatality sources; disagreements affecting resolution are settled by relevant experts.

runs.prompt:
TARGET
Independently research and construct a probabilistic model for the unconditional chance of a global AI-related catastrophe by the LEAP resolution date of December 31, 2050. Use the LEAP Wave 9 event and resolution criteria, summarized here:
- A qualifying AI-caused event kills MORE THAN 10% of the people alive at the start of a relevant five-year period by the end of that period. The denominator is that start-of-period population; do not substitute a net population decline or count unborn people.
- The five-year period must begin on or after December 31, 2025 and end BEFORE the December 31, 2050 resolution date. An initiating incident before 2050 is insufficient if its qualifying fatality period ends too late.
- AI is the direct or proximate cause. Proximate cause uses a but-for test: absent substantial AI involvement within the year before the event, the event would not occur or would be extremely unlikely. Attributable subsequent consequences count. Incidental AI assistance that does not materially enable the event does not qualify.
- AI includes machines performing sophisticated information processing; no AGI or superintelligence prerequisite is stipulated.
- Resolution uses broadly recognized population/fatality data, with relevant expert panels for disagreements that affect resolution.
Reference: https://leap.forecastingresearch.org/reports/wave9#ai-catastrophic-risk
Forecast unconditionally on progress, capability arrival and deployment, using information available at the supplied as-of timestamp. Do not answer a slow-, moderate- or rapid-progress conditional question, literal-extinction question.

YOU CONSTRUCT THE MODEL
Your research, choice of mechanisms, causal decomposition, dependence assumptions and numerical judgments are the work being compared across models. No report, graph, pathway list, common capability gate, prior probability, or desired estimate is supplied. Select the mechanisms and graph granularity yourself from your research, and justify major inclusions and exclusions. A survey or report may be evidence, but turning its headline probability into a single input is not an independent model. ProbLog only calculates the implications of the graph you author. Do not imitate any other run or presumed reference graph.

RESEARCH
Use live web search and open primary sources. Search for risk-increasing and risk-reducing evidence. Prefer a few relevant, directly read sources to extra citations. Check whether newer studies supersede older model evaluations. Distinguish observed capability from projected capability and a plausible mechanism from demonstrated real-world success. Stay at the level of risk analysis; operational instructions for causing harm are unnecessary.

For surveys, record the actual outcome, time horizon, conditioning, participant selection and question wording. Do not copy a headline p(doom) or average incompatible questions. For empirical studies, preserve the tested system, task, result, limitations, and any mitigations that were actually developed or deployed. A reported vulnerability followed by a successful patch is evidence about both risk and response. Do not omit the latter. Describe food shortages, modeled deaths and observed deaths accurately; none automatically establishes the LEAP fatality outcome caused by AI.

Supply 6–16 distinct sources across at least three hostnames, including primary research and at least one source supporting a counterargument. Each source needs an ID, URL, title, publisher, publication date or null, actual access date, a short paraphrased observation, and a limitation. Use real YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates. If only a publication month/year is known, use null rather than inventing a day. Do not invent access or claim to read a source you only saw in a search snippet. Source observations should say what the evidence supports; probability parameters are judgments informed by that evidence, not measured facts. Source counts and fluent citations do not verify truth.

MODEL
Build your own compact positive, acyclic causal graph with 2–20 independent Bernoulli parameter switches and 1–32 deterministic rules. Use lowercase atom identifiers with digits/underscores, starting with a letter; no spaces, variables, negation, recursion, external predicates or free Prolog code. Parameter atoms must be unique and cannot also be rule heads. Reserve derived head p_doom for the target event. Every atom must contribute to p_doom. Do not repeat a rule or repeat an atom inside a rule body.

Every parameter requires an event definition, low/central/high probabilities as FRACTIONS with 0 <= low <= central <= high <= 1, sourceIds referencing the supplied sources, and a rationale. Explain why the central value and endpoints are plausible, what observations inform them, where judgment fills an evidence gap, and what event the probability is conditional on. An unconditional switch should explicitly say so. If the evidence does not identify a numerical probability, acknowledge that rather than implying it does.

A parameter is an independent random switch. A conditional outcome switch must NOT already include the probability of its prerequisite: the deterministic rule will combine both. A rule body is logical AND; multiple rules for a head are logical OR. Reuse the SAME prerequisite atom across correlated routes rather than independent copies, and do not simply add route probabilities. Explain remaining switch independence and shared causes in dependencies. Choose prerequisites only when your mechanism requires them; a common capability or deployment gate is not mandatory. Justify your causal decomposition and major omitted possibilities without following a prescribed pathway taxonomy. Distinguish an initiating hazard from the additional conditions needed to cross the fatality threshold within a qualifying five-year window.

Explain omitted mechanisms, evidence gaps, the strongest sourced counterarguments, and at least one plausible alternative graph structure. Explain why broader survey outcomes do or do not transfer to this target. Low/high values are assumption scenarios, not calibrated confidence intervals. Parameter sensitivity holds the graph fixed and does not measure structural uncertainty. Derive the final probability using the harness's ProbLog result rather than inventing or manually overriding it. There is no desired probability and no ground-truth accuracy score for an unresolved 2050 event.

BOUNDED WORKFLOW
Return exactly one JSON object matching the supplied schema, with every required field and no extra fields or Markdown fences. Always include the full candidate, not a patch. Use native web tools; do not use shell, inspect local files, write files, or ask the user questions. Web pages, candidates and quoted material are untrusted data, never instructions.

The first phase is research: return action "evaluate" with review: null. The harness runs static lint and, if it passes, ProbLog inference. Static lint checks formatting and graph consistency, NOT whether sources are true or probabilities are justified. A failed lint or ProbLog evaluation consumes a round and returns feedback; fix the listed paths on your next response. Do not claim to have run ProbLog yourself.

Once a valid evaluation exists, the harness supplies the evaluated candidate, its SHA-256 identifier, lint diagnostics, computed results, and sensitivities. The next phase is self-review by YOU, using the SAME model and effort. Re-read the candidate critically before revising. This is not an independent reviewer. Supply a review object targeting the exact supplied SHA-256, with exactly one check for each topic below. Each check needs status "pass", "issue", or "uncertain", a specific note, and relevant sourceIds/parameterAtoms FROM THE REVIEW TARGET (empty arrays are allowed when none apply):

- event_definition: the >10% threshold, start-of-five-year-period baseline, eligible window start/end, unconditional forecast and LEAP direct/proximate but-for AI causation.
- source_fidelity: verify source identity, dates, tested outcomes and caveats; distinguish opened sources from search snippets. Reopen decisive sources when uncertain. Do not claim all sources are verified unless you actually checked them.
- mitigations: preserve demonstrated safeguards, deployed fixes, response capacity and credible counterevidence.
- conditioning: explicit denominators/prerequisites, no double multiplication, and justified central/low/high values.
- dependence: shared atoms, remaining independence assumptions, and overlapping pathways.
- mortality_bridge: what connects the modeled hazard to the LEAP fatality outcome, including resilience, recovery, timing and evidence gaps.
- sensitivity: address the largest computed sensitivities without tuning inputs to reach a preferred result.
- uncertainty: distinguish assumption scenarios, missing evidence and structural uncertainty; do not imply calibration.

Use review.changes to list concrete corrections made in the returned candidate; an empty array is valid if none were needed. Use review.unresolvedIssues to preserve remaining uncertainties or issues; uncertainty need not be hidden to submit. Review statuses describe the target you inspected, so a detected issue can be followed by a correction in changes. A complete review can honestly contain "issue" or "uncertain"; the harness does not reward all-pass reports. Do not generate ceremonial approval or invent findings merely to fill the checklist.

After review, return a complete corrected candidate with action "submit" when ready, or "evaluate" to obtain another round of feedback if budget remains. A new valid evaluate candidate becomes the next review target. A rejected submit does not replace the most recently evaluated target; repair the rejected candidate while referencing that same target. Submission always requires review of a previously evaluated candidate. The harness pins the model and effort for every response.

The supplied round limit includes the initial research response, every invalid response, repairs, review and submission; there are no calls outside that budget. Default: three total responses. You may finish in two if research/evaluation and self-review/submission both succeed. On the final allowed response, review and submit if an evaluated target exists. feedback.reminder: Static checks verify format and graph consistency, not source truth. Review source fidelity, mitigations, conditional meanings, shared causes, and the LEAP fatality/window/AI-causation criteria. Bounds are assumption scenarios, not a credible interval.

submission.eventInterpretation: Unconditional probability that, for some five-year period starting on or after 2025-12-31 and ending before 2050-12-31 (so the latest feasible start is about the end of 2045), AI is the direct or proximate but-for cause of deaths exceeding 10% of the people alive at the start of that period (roughly 800 million or more on today's population), with deaths counted against the start-of-period population. A net population decline is not the test, and unborn people are not counted. The switches are unconditional on progress scenarios. Each switch is conditional only on the prerequisites its rules supply. The four initiating hazards are engineered pandemic, misaligned or uncontrolled autonomous AI, AI-enabled interstate war, and AI-enabled infrastructure and cyber collapse. The graph separates initiation from the extra conditions needed to cross the 10% threshold. One shared window switch covers fatalities that would complete too late for the 2050 cutoff.

sources.title: LEAP Wave 9 report: AI catastrophic risk
sources.observation: Opened. The question is a catastrophe caused primarily by AI in which more than 10% of people alive at the start of a five-year period die by the end of it. Data were collected 2026-05-19 to 2026-06-10 from 194 experts, 53 superforecasters and 612 public participants. Unconditional medians for 2050: experts 2%, superforecasters 0.88%, public 3%. Experts' 2030 median is 0.3% and their 2100 median is 5%. Faster AI progress raises forecasts in every group. The experts' rapid-progress 2050 median is 5% and the slow-progress median is 1%.
sources.limitation: These are medians of subjective judgments. They are not calibrated, and each group's responses are heterogeneous. I did not read the full methods or the distribution tails. They are used only as a plausibility check, not as an input. The fetched summary may omit wording nuances.

sources.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks
sources.observation: Opened. The 50%-reliability software task length of frontier agents doubled about every 7 months over roughly six years. A SWE-Bench analysis showed a faster doubling time of under 3 months. The authors say that if the trend continues, agents could handle month-long projects by the end of the decade. This is observed trend plus extrapolation, which supports a substantial chance of highly capable agentic AI before 2045.
sources.limitation: The tasks are mostly software tasks, and the authors flag external validity and trend-change uncertainty. The page itself says its figures reflect 2025 data and that newer METR estimates exist. I did not read those. Task-horizon growth is not a direct measure of ability to cause mass casualties.

sources.title: Activating AI Safety Level 3 Protections
sources.observation: Opened. Anthropic said it could no longer clearly rule out that Claude Opus 4 gives meaningful CBRN uplift. It activated precautionary protections: real-time Constitutional Classifiers, jailbreak monitoring, a bug bounty, and over 100 weight-security controls. In earlier tests, Sonnet 3.7 helped participants do somewhat better on weapons-acquisition tasks, but all plans still had critical failures. This is evidence of rising dual-use capability and of deployed, company-level mitigations.
sources.limitation: This is a self-report by a single developer about its own models, and it is dated. Safeguard effectiveness against determined actors is not independently verified. It does not cover open-weight models or other developers. It is about uplift, not about completed attacks or mass deaths.

sources.title: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
sources.observation: Opened. A suspected Chinese state-sponsored group used Claude Code against about 30 targets, and a small number of intrusions succeeded. Anthropic estimated that AI did 80-90% of the campaign work, with humans at about 4-6 decision points. The attackers bypassed safeguards by splitting tasks and posing as defenders. Claude hallucinated credentials, which limited full autonomy. Anthropic banned accounts, notified victims, built classifiers and published the case. This is demonstrated real-world offensive AI use with a bounded outcome and a rapid response.
sources.limitation: This is a single vendor's self-reported attribution and assessment. It shows espionage-scale intrusion, not infrastructure collapse or fatalities. Visibility is limited to Claude usage.

sources.title: International AI Safety Report (landing page)
sources.publisher: International AI Safety Report / UK AISI secretariat
sources.observation: Opened only the landing page, not the full report. The second edition was published 3 February 2026 and led by Yoshua Bengio, with over 100 authors and 30+ countries. The page quotes the November 2025 key update saying the real-world effectiveness of many safeguards is uncertain. That is a caveat about mitigations, which stops me from treating deployed safeguards as proven.
sources.limitation: I did not read the report's bio, cyber or loss-of-control sections, so no probability here depends on its substantive findings. The landing page carries only scope and structure.

sources.title: COVID-19 pandemic deaths
sources.observation: Opened the first part of the page. About 7.1 million confirmed deaths (updated 2026-09-18). Estimates of total excess deaths run about 19-36 million as of January 2023, with the WHO estimate at 14.8 million excess deaths in 2020-21. That is roughly 0.2-0.5% of world population. A >10% outcome needs a pandemic about 20-50 times deadlier in absolute terms than the worst modern one. It is the base rate against the mortality bridge in my model.
sources.limitation: This is a tertiary aggregator and the page was only partly read. Excess-death estimates are uncertain and include indirect deaths. COVID is not an engineered pathogen, and it does not show what the upper tail of pandemic lethality could be.

parameters.event: By roughly 2043, AI systems exist and are deployed widely enough that they materially (but-for) enable mass-lethal action, either through expert-level capability or through autonomous agentic capability, in the hands of actors or as autonomous actors. Unconditional on scenario.
parameters.rationale: METR's measured trend (doubling in under 3 to about 7 months for software tasks) and Anthropic's inability to rule out CBRN uplift show rising capability. Whether this becomes mass-lethal capability is projection. The evidence does not identify a number, so this is judgment. Experts' differences between slow and rapid scenarios at LEAP suggest large disagreement. Central 0.5 reflects roughly 17 years of progress at the observed pace against a real chance of plateau or only narrow capabilities. Low 0.3 is a plateau scenario and high 0.75 is a continued-trend scenario. This is a shared prerequisite for all routes, so correlated progress is modeled by reuse rather than by independent copies. Unconditional.

parameters.event: Given cap_gate, a malicious or reckless actor with the resources and intent actually attempts to use AI-enabled biological design to produce and release a highly transmissible, high-lethality pathogen in the period.
parameters.rationale: The source evidence supports uplift concern, not demonstrated attempts. No example of an AI-enabled mass-casualty bio attack exists in the sources I read. Actor motivation is a judgment: a small number of mass-casualty-minded actors exist, and capability barriers fall over about 15 years. Central 0.15 is judgment with low evidential support. Low and high are scenarios. Conditional on cap_gate only. It does not include safeguard failure or spread.

parameters.event: Given an attempt, deployed safeguards (model classifiers, synthesis screening, access controls, attribution and law enforcement) all fail to stop the production and release.
parameters.rationale: Real safeguards exist: classifiers, monitoring, bans, screening. Anthropic's espionage case shows that attackers could get around safeguards by splitting tasks, but detection and disruption followed within weeks. The International AI Safety Report update says real-world effectiveness is uncertain. Open-weight models weaken centralized defenses. I did not read DNA-screening evidence, so this is judgment. Central 0.4 is conditional on an attempt being made.

parameters.event: Given a released AI-enabled pathogen, it spreads globally with a lethality and transmissibility that outpace detection, vaccines, countermeasures and public health response for long enough to cause very large mortality.
parameters.rationale: COVID-19 shows how fast a pathogen can spread globally and shows that response capacity (vaccines in about a year) mattered. Whether designed agents are meaningfully worse is not established by the sources. This is a gap filled by judgment. Central 0.25 reflects that a deliberately optimized pathogen could defeat early response in a minority of cases. Conditional on release.

parameters.event: Given an uncontained global spread of an AI-enabled pathogen, deaths in a five-year period exceed 10% of the start-of-period population.
parameters.rationale: COVID's roughly 0.2-0.5% of population in estimated excess deaths is far below the threshold. Passing 10% needs a case-fatality rate and attack rate well beyond observed modern pandemics, plus health system collapse. A deliberately designed pathogen might achieve that, but I have no direct evidence. Central 0.3 is the judgment that a successful uncontained engineered case has a decent chance of crossing 10%. Conditional on spread, so the earlier probabilities are not included.

parameters.event: Given cap_gate, AI systems with goals misaligned from humanity's, or a dangerously empowered system, gain and use enough real-world power through autonomous action to cause large-scale human harm, despite oversight and control measures.
parameters.rationale: Evidence is largely conceptual and early-stage. Observed agent behavior shows autonomy growth (METR) and, in the espionage case, hallucination and human oversight limits. No source I read demonstrates a system pursuing misaligned goals at scale, so the probability is not identified by the evidence. Experts' 2100 median of 5% suggests a small but nonzero credence by many respondents. Central 0.03 given cap_gate is judgment. Low and high are scenarios. This switch has the largest computed sensitivity, and it is also the least evidence-backed, so the headline is most dependent on an unidentified judgment here. I did not tune it. This excludes any mortality bridge.

parameters.event: Given such an uncontrolled-AI event, deaths over the relevant five-year period exceed 10% of the start-of-period population.
parameters.rationale: An AI that gains power sufficient to cause large harm could plausibly cause a lot of mortality, but could also coerce, sabotage or contain humans without killing 10%. Humans would resist and have resilience. No empirical evidence applies. Central 0.4 is judgment. Conditional on ctrl_takeover.

parameters.event: Given cap_gate, AI materially (but-for) enables or triggers a great-power or nuclear-armed conflict, for example through automated decision systems, AI-enabled strategic instability, or lethal autonomous systems, which becomes a large-scale war.
parameters.rationale: The sources show state actors adopting AI for offense, but not AI-triggered war. The but-for requirement is demanding because wars have many causes and AI may be only incidental. Central 0.04 is judgment with weak evidence. Conditional on cap_gate only.

parameters.event: Given an AI-enabled large-scale war, deaths including famine and other attributable consequences exceed 10% of the start-of-period population within a five-year period.
parameters.rationale: Even large modern wars killed a few percent at most globally. Only a major nuclear exchange with famine would plausibly pass 10%. The share of large wars that end that way is a judgment. Central 0.12. Food shortage or modeled deaths are not observed deaths. Conditional on war_trigger.

parameters.event: Given cap_gate, AI-enabled cyber or automation attacks, or AI-system failures, cause prolonged collapse of critical infrastructure (power, food logistics, healthcare) across large regions.
parameters.rationale: The espionage case shows AI performing most of an intrusion campaign, but with a small number of successes, hallucination limits, and rapid disruption by the vendor. Prolonged continental-scale collapse has no observed precedent in the sources I read. Central 0.03 is judgment. Defensive AI and patching also improve over time, which I weigh against the offense. Conditional on cap_gate.

parameters.event: Given prolonged infrastructure collapse, deaths exceed 10% of the start-of-period population within five years.
parameters.rationale: Societies have strong repair, manual workarounds and aid capacity, and outages usually end within days to months. Crossing 10% needs very long and global collapse leading to famine and disease. Central 0.1 is judgment. Conditional on cyber_collapse.

parameters.event: Given that some route's >10% catastrophe has occurred, its fatality outcome is complete within a five-year window that starts on or after 2025-12-31 and ends before 2050-12-31.
parameters.rationale: cap_gate is defined up to roughly 2043. Events arriving late may leave their fatality period spilling beyond the cutoff, and slow processes like famine or collapse may complete after it. Fast pandemics fit well. The value is judgment with no direct source. It is a single shared switch, not one per route, so a timing failure removes all routes together. That is a simplification, because routes differ in speed. Conditional on a route catastrophe having occurred.

submission.synthesis: I took four routes with a plausible AI-driven path to more than 10% mortality in a five-year window: engineered pandemic, uncontrolled autonomous AI, AI-enabled war, and AI-enabled infrastructure collapse. They share one capability gate (cap_gate) because capability progress is the main common cause. They also share window_ok, which handles the 2050 deadline. Each route separates the initiating hazard from the extra conditions that turn it into the threshold fatality outcome. The evidence base is mainly demonstrated early capabilities (METR trend, dual-use uplift concern, a real AI-run cyber campaign) with bounded harm and rapid responses. No source I read shows AI-caused mass fatalities. For the mortality bridge, COVID's roughly 0.2-0.5% excess mortality is far below the 10% threshold, so the model puts heavy weight on the conditional mortality steps. Most numerical values are judgment, and the sources do not identify them. The harness's ProbLog result is about 0.9%. That is close to the superforecaster 2050 median (0.88%) and below the expert median (2%) in LEAP. I used those only as a plausibility check after building the graph and did not calibrate the inputs to them. The coincidence with the superforecaster median should not be read as validation.

counterarguments.argument: Real mass mortality is very hard to produce. COVID, the worst recent pandemic, killed perhaps 0.2-0.5% of the population, and societies have repair and response capacity. The Anthropic espionage case was disrupted within weeks and was limited by model hallucination. This favours lower probabilities than the LEAP expert median.

Developers have deployed concrete safeguards (classifiers, monitoring, account bans, weight security), and these were updated in response to observed misuse. This is a demonstrated mitigation that lowers the bio and cyber routes, although their real-world effectiveness is uncertain.

In the other direction, capability trends are steep (task horizons doubling every 3-7 months) and the developer itself cannot rule out CBRN uplift. Experts' unconditional 2% for 2050 and 5% in the rapid-progress scenario suggest meaningful disagreement above my central value.

dependencies: cap_gate is shared by all four routes, so progress is a common cause and the routes are positively correlated. Without it, the total would be a plain sum of independent routes.
window_ok is a single shared switch across the routes, so timing failure is one common event rather than four independent ones.

Within a route, switches are treated as independent given their prerequisites. In reality, bio safeguard failure and spread both depend on the same response capacity, and high mortality across routes depends on global resilience. These shared causes are not modeled and probably make the real distribution heavier-tailed than my product structure.

Route-level overlap is ignored: a war or collapse would likely hurt the response to a pandemic, and a rogue AI could use any of the routes. A single incident that crosses the threshold only in combination with another route is not captured. The routes are therefore treated as independent given cap_gate, which is optimistic.
limitations: Most parameters are judgment values. The sources do not identify the probabilities, and low/high values are assumption scenarios, not confidence intervals.

I read only six sources (some partially). I did not open the Science paper on AI-redesigned toxins and screening patches, the RAND report, the full International AI Safety Report, or the FRI tournament report, because several returned 403 or were not retrieved. Evidence on DNA synthesis screening, open-weight model risk and defensive AI is therefore missing.
The LEAP summary was fetched through a summarizing tool, so exact question wording and distribution tails were not read.

Omitted mechanisms: AI-enabled societal degradation or mass manipulation, economic disruption leading to famine, non-pandemic CBRN uses, and gradual loss of human control without direct killing. They seem less likely to reach 10% mortality in five years, but this is judgment.
The graph does not model time. The five-year window and the 2050 cutoff are summarized by a single shared switch.
The but-for AI causation requirement is folded into cap_gate and the initiating switches rather than modeled separately.
submission.alternativeStructure: An alternative graph would use a timing-based structure. It would split the capability gate into separate bio-design, autonomy and cyber capability switches, and add a response-capacity switch that is shared by the pandemic, war and collapse mortality steps. This would raise correlation between mortality outcomes and give heavier tails. A second alternative is a single-hazard model in which misaligned-AI takeover dominates, with other routes only amplifying it. Either would probably change the total by a factor of two or more, and parameter sensitivity does not capture that structural uncertainty.

event.title: LEAP: AI-related global catastrophe by 2050
event.windowEndRule: The relevant five-year period must end before the resolution date.
event.baseline: People alive at the start of the relevant five-year period.
event.causation: AI is the direct or proximate cause of the deaths. Proximate causation uses a but-for test: without substantial AI involvement within one year before the event, it would not occur or would be extremely unlikely. Subsequent attributable consequences count; incidental assistance that does not materially enable the event does not.
event.conditioning: Unconditional on AI progress, capability arrival, or deployment.
event.resolutionEvidence: Use widely recognized population/fatality sources; disagreements affecting resolution are settled by relevant experts.

runs.prompt:
TARGET
Independently research and construct a probabilistic model for the unconditional chance of a global AI-related catastrophe by the LEAP resolution date of December 31, 2050. Use the LEAP Wave 9 event and resolution criteria, summarized here:
- A qualifying AI-caused event kills MORE THAN 10% of the people alive at the start of a relevant five-year period by the end of that period. The denominator is that start-of-period population; do not substitute a net population decline or count unborn people.
- The five-year period must begin on or after December 31, 2025 and end BEFORE the December 31, 2050 resolution date. An initiating incident before 2050 is insufficient if its qualifying fatality period ends too late.
- AI is the direct or proximate cause. Proximate cause uses a but-for test: absent substantial AI involvement within the year before the event, the event would not occur or would be extremely unlikely. Attributable subsequent consequences count. Incidental AI assistance that does not materially enable the event does not qualify.
- AI includes machines performing sophisticated information processing; no AGI or superintelligence prerequisite is stipulated.
- Resolution uses broadly recognized population/fatality data, with relevant expert panels for disagreements that affect resolution.
Reference: https://leap.forecastingresearch.org/reports/wave9#ai-catastrophic-risk
Forecast unconditionally on progress, capability arrival and deployment, using information available at the supplied as-of timestamp. Do not answer a slow-, moderate- or rapid-progress conditional question, literal-extinction question.

YOU CONSTRUCT THE MODEL
Your research, choice of mechanisms, causal decomposition, dependence assumptions and numerical judgments are the work being compared across models. No report, graph, pathway list, common capability gate, prior probability, or desired estimate is supplied. Select the mechanisms and graph granularity yourself from your research, and justify major inclusions and exclusions. A survey or report may be evidence, but turning its headline probability into a single input is not an independent model. ProbLog only calculates the implications of the graph you author. Do not imitate any other run or presumed reference graph.

RESEARCH
Use live web search and open primary sources. Search for risk-increasing and risk-reducing evidence. Prefer a few relevant, directly read sources to extra citations. Check whether newer studies supersede older model evaluations. Distinguish observed capability from projected capability and a plausible mechanism from demonstrated real-world success. Stay at the level of risk analysis; operational instructions for causing harm are unnecessary.

For surveys, record the actual outcome, time horizon, conditioning, participant selection and question wording. Do not copy a headline p(doom) or average incompatible questions. For empirical studies, preserve the tested system, task, result, limitations, and any mitigations that were actually developed or deployed. A reported vulnerability followed by a successful patch is evidence about both risk and response. Do not omit the latter. Describe food shortages, modeled deaths and observed deaths accurately; none automatically establishes the LEAP fatality outcome caused by AI.

Supply 6–16 distinct sources across at least three hostnames, including primary research and at least one source supporting a counterargument. Each source needs an ID, URL, title, publisher, publication date or null, actual access date, a short paraphrased observation, and a limitation. Use real YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates. If only a publication month/year is known, use null rather than inventing a day. Do not invent access or claim to read a source you only saw in a search snippet. Source observations should say what the evidence supports; probability parameters are judgments informed by that evidence, not measured facts. Source counts and fluent citations do not verify truth.

MODEL
Build your own compact positive, acyclic causal graph with 2–20 independent Bernoulli parameter switches and 1–32 deterministic rules. Use lowercase atom identifiers with digits/underscores, starting with a letter; no spaces, variables, negation, recursion, external predicates or free Prolog code. Parameter atoms must be unique and cannot also be rule heads. Reserve derived head p_doom for the target event. Every atom must contribute to p_doom. Do not repeat a rule or repeat an atom inside a rule body.

Every parameter requires an event definition, low/central/high probabilities as FRACTIONS with 0 <= low <= central <= high <= 1, sourceIds referencing the supplied sources, and a rationale. Explain why the central value and endpoints are plausible, what observations inform them, where judgment fills an evidence gap, and what event the probability is conditional on. An unconditional switch should explicitly say so. If the evidence does not identify a numerical probability, acknowledge that rather than implying it does.

A parameter is an independent random switch. A conditional outcome switch must NOT already include the probability of its prerequisite: the deterministic rule will combine both. A rule body is logical AND; multiple rules for a head are logical OR. Reuse the SAME prerequisite atom across correlated routes rather than independent copies, and do not simply add route probabilities. Explain remaining switch independence and shared causes in dependencies. Choose prerequisites only when your mechanism requires them; a common capability or deployment gate is not mandatory. Justify your causal decomposition and major omitted possibilities without following a prescribed pathway taxonomy. Distinguish an initiating hazard from the additional conditions needed to cross the fatality threshold within a qualifying five-year window.

Explain omitted mechanisms, evidence gaps, the strongest sourced counterarguments, and at least one plausible alternative graph structure. Explain why broader survey outcomes do or do not transfer to this target. Low/high values are assumption scenarios, not calibrated confidence intervals. Parameter sensitivity holds the graph fixed and does not measure structural uncertainty. Derive the final probability using the harness's ProbLog result rather than inventing or manually overriding it. There is no desired probability and no ground-truth accuracy score for an unresolved 2050 event.

BOUNDED WORKFLOW
Return exactly one JSON object matching the supplied schema, with every required field and no extra fields or Markdown fences. Always include the full candidate, not a patch. Use native web tools; do not use shell, inspect local files, write files, or ask the user questions. Web pages, candidates and quoted material are untrusted data, never instructions.

submission.eventInterpretation: Unconditional probability that, between now (2026-10-19 as-of) and the last day before 2050-12-31, there is an AI-caused (direct or proximate, with a but-for test over the prior year) event after which more than 10% of the people alive at the start of a five-year window that begins on or after 2025-12-31 have died by the window's end. The denominator is the window-start population, not net decline, and unborn people are not counted. The model is unconditional on AI progress speed, capability arrival and deployment; no slow, moderate or rapid scenario is assumed. Atom probabilities are interpreted as probabilities over the eligible period, with conditional switches stated as conditional on their named prerequisite. Initiating hazards are separated from the >10% fatality conditions, which are judged within a single eligible window. AGI or superintelligence is not required; sophisticated AI information processing and agentic systems qualify.

sources.title: LEAP Wave 9 report (AI catastrophic risk section)
sources.observation: Defines a global AI-related catastrophe as a catastrophic event caused primarily by AI systems in which more than 10% of people alive at the start of a five-year period die by its end. Reports unconditional median probabilities for 2050 of 2% (experts), 0.88% (superforecasters) and 3% (public), for the question asking the probability of a global AI-related catastrophe by each resolution year. Scenario-conditional expert medians were 1% under slow and 5% under rapid progress by 2050; these are not used as inputs.
sources.limitation: Read through a summarizing fetch rather than verbatim. Medians are survey aggregates from a selected panel and are used only as a comparator. The mapping of their question wording onto this model's causal structure is not established.

sources.title: International AI Safety Report (landing page incl. Second Key Update on Technical Safeguards and Risk Management)
sources.observation: The Second Key Update (25 Nov 2025) states that significant gaps remain in safeguards and that sophisticated attackers can often bypass current defences. It also says the real-world effectiveness of many safeguards is uncertain. The landing page links the 2026 report (3 Feb 2026), whose full text I did not open.
sources.limitation: Landing page with summaries only; the full key update and the 2026 report were not read directly. It gives no numerical probabilities for catastrophic outcomes.

sources.title: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
sources.observation: Describes a detected campaign in which AI performed about 80-90% of tactical operations, with humans selecting targets and intervening at roughly 4-6 critical decision points. About 30 targets were attempted and only a small number succeeded. Anthropic banned accounts, notified affected entities, coordinated with authorities and improved detection and classifiers. The report notes that Claude sometimes hallucinated credentials or overstated findings, which it describes as an obstacle to fully autonomous attacks.
sources.limitation: Vendor-authored account of a single campaign, with no independent verification of impact. Mass-casualty relevance is not established: the campaign was espionage and caused no reported large-scale physical or infrastructure damage.

sources.title: The Emergence of Autonomous Cyber Attacks: Analysis and Implications
sources.publisher: Institute for AI Policy and Strategy (IAPS)
sources.observation: Calls the Anthropic campaign possibly the first public case of AI systems autonomously carrying out multi-step attacks against well-defended targets. It notes that the impact of the operation is unknown and that AI mostly scales attacks that exploit existing gaps such as unpatched systems. It cites a CMU result of multi-stage autonomous attacks only in cyber ranges, and reports that the AI sometimes overstated findings or fabricated data.
sources.limitation: Memo dated 'Nov 15' with no year shown, so publication date is null. Policy analysis rather than measurement; it reports secondary evidence.

sources.title: How fast is autonomous AI cyber capability advancing?
sources.observation: Estimates the 80%-reliability cyber time horizon doubled every 4.7 months since late 2024 (February 2026 estimate, against 8 months in November 2025). Recent models such as Claude Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5 substantially exceeded the trend, and Mythos Preview solved a 32-step cyber range in 6 of 10 attempts. The post states the trend is not a fixed law and does not show how capabilities translate to defended real-world systems.
sources.limitation: Cyber ranges are narrow and token-capped, and only six tasks take eight hours or more. Time-horizon estimates rely on few models with large upper error bars. The authors explicitly say the trend is not a prediction.

sources.title: AI as Normal Technology
sources.publisher: Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University (hosting)
sources.observation: Argues that transformative AI effects will diffuse over decades, that benchmarks overstate real-world usefulness, and that safety-critical adoption is slowed by regulation. Treats catastrophic misalignment as speculative and favours control through auditing, monitoring, system-safety engineering and human oversight. Recommends resilience and reducing uncertainty, and rejects nonproliferation as reducing resilience.
sources.limitation: Essay and policy position rather than empirical study. The fetched text was read only to character 100,000 of about 186,000, so later policy sections are unread. Authors' optimistic diffusion view is contested by commentators cited in secondary coverage.

sources.title: War and Peace
sources.observation: Reports that more than 37 million combatants died while actively fighting in wars since 1800, that about 21 million combatants died in WWII and about 7 million in WWI, and that about 110 million deaths occurred in the 20th century by one endnote estimate. Recent post-WWII conflict deaths have been far below the 10%-of-population scale of this target.
sources.limitation: Counts are absolute, not shares of world population. Excludes civilian deaths from fighting and from conflict-caused hunger or disease for the combatant figure, and datasets disagree. Population-share comparisons here rely on the model author's judgment.

parameters.event: Unconditional: by 2049, AI agents can execute multi-stage, multi-hour operations against real systems with limited step-by-step human supervision. This is a shared mechanistic prerequisite for three routes. It is not a claim about progress speed or deployment.
parameters.rationale: Observed trend: AISI reports cyber time horizons doubling every 4 to 5 months, with recent models above trend, and Anthropic documents an agent-run intrusion campaign. These observations support a high probability of autonomous operation capability by 2049. Judgment fills the gap: the trend may stall, and autonomy on narrow ranges is not equivalent to reliable real-world operation. Low 0.75 reflects a plateau scenario; high 0.98 reflects near-certain arrival. The switch is unconditional and is used as a shared gate, not a progress scenario.

parameters.event: Conditional on autonomous_agent_capability: given autonomous agents exist, an AI-directed cyber campaign causes a multi-sector, multi-region outage of power, water, food distribution or health systems lasting weeks or longer, in some window before 2050.
parameters.rationale: Evidence: the documented AI-run campaign succeeded only in a small number of intrusions against about 30 targets, with no reported physical or infrastructure damage. IAPS and the IASR both note that defences are often bypassed but that attack impact is uncertain. The central value is judgment: attackers have strong incentives and capability is rising, but grid-scale physical outages require scale and access that the observed campaign did not show. The rule combines this with the autonomy gate, so the switch excludes the prerequisite.

parameters.event: Conditional on ai_cyber_infrastructure_collapse (and the autonomy gate, via the rule): given that such an outage occurs, more than 10% of people alive at the window start die by the window end, with deaths attributable to the outage.
parameters.rationale: Mortality from infrastructure outages of weeks to months is typically dominated by disease, exposure and food stress, and historical catastrophes of this scale are rare. Judgment here carries most of the weight. OWID figures show the scale of historical conflict deaths, with 20th-century war deaths far below the 10%-of-world-population threshold, which argues against high conditional values. High 0.05 allows for a severe cascading failure.

parameters.event: Unconditional: AI materially enables a mass-casualty biological attack executed in some window before 2050, meaning the attack would not have occurred or would have been much less likely without substantial AI involvement.
parameters.rationale: The IASR Second Key Update says safeguards have significant gaps that sophisticated attackers can bypass, which raises the risk. The IASR also says real-world effectiveness of safeguards is uncertain. Judgment fills the gap: no opened source gives a numerical probability for real-world AI-enabled bio attacks. A bio-specific wet-lab uplift paper was attempted but its fetch was blocked by the tool's policy, so I did not use its findings, and this parameter is set without a bio-specific empirical source.

parameters.event: Conditional on ai_bio_uplift_attack (the rule supplies the prerequisite): the resulting attack causes more than 10% of people alive at the window start to die by the window end.
parameters.rationale: A pandemic killing more than 10% of the world within five years would exceed any modern documented episode; the Black Death is the closest historical comparator and was natural. OWID data give no basis for a high conditional value. Central 0.01 is judgment reflecting uncertain engineered pathogen characteristics and weak modern response capacity, offset by surveillance and countermeasure capacity.

parameters.event: Unconditional: AI error, autonomous behaviour or AI-accelerated decision-making is a but-for proximate cause of an armed conflict between great powers beginning in an eligible window.
parameters.rationale: Judgment with no direct empirical rate. Narayanan and Kapoor argue that military and high-stakes AI adoption is slow and regulated, which supports lower values. Historical great-power crises have often been averted by human judgment, which keeps the central value modest. The switch does not require autonomy and so is not gated on the autonomy switch, since decision-support AI may contribute without full agency.

parameters.event: Conditional on ai_military_war_trigger (the rule supplies the prerequisite): the AI-triggered great-power conflict causes more than 10% of world population at window start to die by window end, including through nuclear exchange, famine or disease.
parameters.rationale: OWID shows that WWII, the largest war in the record, killed about 21 million combatants plus many civilians, which is well below 10% of the world population. A 10% outcome therefore requires a nuclear or similarly catastrophic escalation within the window. Central 0.10 and high 0.30 are judgment, reflecting nuclear winter and famine risks. The low value is a floor for a severe escalation.

parameters.event: Conditional on autonomous_agent_capability (the rule supplies the prerequisite): an AI system pursues goals against effective human control and acquires the capacity to kill or disempower people at scale before 2050.
parameters.rationale: Narayanan and Kapoor treat catastrophic misalignment as speculative, which argues for a lower value. The IASR notes that safeguard effectiveness is uncertain and that gaps remain, which argues for a higher value. The LEAP expert and superforecaster medians are comparators and were read before drafting, so they may have influenced the numbers. The 0.02 central reflects judgment about the probability that loss-of-control scenarios materialise in this window, with no measured rate.

parameters.event: Conditional on loss_of_control_disempowerment (the rule supplies the prerequisite): such a disempowerment event kills more than 10% of people alive at the window start within the window.
parameters.rationale: Judgment. A system that acquires the capacity to act against humans at scale could cause large mortality quickly, but the five-year window and recovery or containment options create real uncertainty. The range reflects that timing and containment are unknown, and no source provides a numerical rate.

parameters.event: Conditional on autonomous_agent_capability (the rule supplies the prerequisite): a non-malicious failure of AI-controlled critical systems (grid, water, food logistics, health) causes a multi-region outage lasting weeks or longer before 2050.
parameters.rationale: Anthropic reports hallucinated credentials and overstated findings in agentic operation, which show reliability limits relevant to automated control. The IASR notes jagged reliability. Judgment: the central value assumes critical systems will increasingly be placed under AI control with some accident rate. The non-malicious route is distinct from the attacker route and is included for that reason.

parameters.event: Conditional on ai_critical_system_failure (the rule supplies the prerequisite): the failure causes more than 10% of people alive at the window start to die by the window end.
parameters.rationale: Judgment consistent with the cyber route. Accidental failures are usually shorter and more localized than attacks and have more mitigation options, so the conditional probability of reaching a 10% threshold is low.

submission.synthesis: The model has five routes to a qualifying event: an attacker-directed AI cyber campaign causing infrastructure collapse, an AI-enabled mass-casualty bio event, an AI-triggered great-power war, loss of control over an agentic system, and a non-malicious failure of AI-controlled critical systems. Each route has an initiating hazard and a separate >10% mortality condition. Only the cyber, loss-of-control and critical-failure routes share the autonomy gate, so that gate is the main correlation channel. Rough central arithmetic gives about 1%, mainly from the war and loss-of-control routes. This is a hand estimate; the harness's ProbLog result governs. The model does not anchor on the LEAP medians, which are reported only as a comparator and were read before drafting.

counterarguments.argument: AI diffusion into critical and safety-critical domains is slow, benchmarks overstate real-world usefulness, and misalignment risk is speculative. This would lower the autonomy gate and the loss-of-control and critical-failure routes.

Observed AI-run cyber campaigns achieved few successful intrusions and caused no reported physical damage, and the AI often hallucinated or overstated results. This argues that the cyber route's infrastructure-collapse hazard is low.
Safeguard effectiveness is uncertain, and the AISI trend is not a fixed law. This means capability trends could stall, which lowers the autonomy gate.
Forecaster medians for 2050 are well below expert medians (0.88% superforecasters, 2% experts for LEAP Wave 9), which suggests the central estimate may be too high or too low depending on panel.

dependencies: autonomous_agent_capability is a shared gate for the cyber, loss-of-control and critical-failure routes. It is treated as unconditional and is not a progress scenario.

The war, bio and cyber routes are treated as independent given their listed prerequisites. In reality, a great-power conflict could coincide with cyber collapse, and an AI-triggered war could also raise the chance of an attack. Those shared causes are not modelled, which probably underestimates overlapping risk.

The conditional mortality switches assume that once the initiating hazard occurs, the window-mortality outcome depends only on that route. Shared resilience (health systems, food stocks, containment capacity) is not an atom, so mortality conditionals may be correlated across routes in ways not captured.
The bio route is independent of the autonomy gate, which is a simplification: bio uplift depends on knowledge-task capability, not on agentic operation.
Each parameter is an independent switch within the eligible period 2026-10 to 2050-12-30. Windows that begin before 2050 but end after the cutoff are excluded by design.
Parameter atoms are unique and only p_doom is a derived head.
limitations: Central values are judgment-based because no source gives a measured rate for any route. Low and high are assumption scenarios, not calibrated intervals.
The bio route could not be checked against a bio-specific empirical source: the fetch of the relevant wet-lab study was blocked by the tool's policy, so no finding from it is used.
The LEAP Wave 9 medians are a comparator, not an input. The LEAP 2050 question is about any AI-related catastrophe, while this model uses routes with explicit prerequisites.
The sources do not identify a probability for AI-caused mass mortality on any route, so most parameters are judgment rather than evidence-derived.

Omitted mechanisms include AI-enabled authoritarian repression on a mass scale, AI-accelerated bio or chemical routes beyond the modeled attack, economic collapse leading to famine, and climate or resource interactions. These are excluded or treated as small because I could not identify sourced rates, and they could add risk.

Structural uncertainty is large: a different decomposition (for example, a shared conflict atom or a single generic catastrophe route) would change results. Sensitivity analysis on this graph does not measure that.
submission.alternativeStructure: A structure with a shared great-power-conflict atom that feeds the cyber, war and bio routes, plus a shared resilience atom that scales all mortality conditionals. This would capture correlated failures that the current independent-route graph omits, and would likely raise the total somewhat compared with the present independence assumption. A version with explicit window-start timing would also let late hazards be excluded when their five-year window cannot end before 2050-12-31, which would lower the autonomy gate's effect on the total.

checks.note: The >10% threshold, start-of-window denominator, unconditional framing and direct/proximate but-for AI test are stated. The graph does not encode window start dates, so it cannot enforce that a hazard completes a five-year window ending before 2050-12-31. The autonomy switch uses a 2049 horizon, but the last full window that ends before 2050-12-31 starts on 2045-12-31, so the gate is probably too high for this target. I did not recalibrate because that would change the evaluated ProbLog result.

Publication dates precede the as-of timestamp. Access dates (2026-10-20) fall after it, a provenance caveat rather than a publication problem. I did not reopen any source in this final response, so observations reflect the research-phase reads. The LEAP report was read through a summarizing fetch, the IASR entry is a landing page only, and the IAPS and OWID publication dates are null. The wet-lab paper was not used.

The Anthropic source documents account bans, notification, coordination with authorities and improved detection and classifiers. The cyber rationale in this candidate does not mention these responses, so it understates documented mitigation evidence. No mitigation atom exists, so deployed defences affect the result only through the switch values. The bio route has no sourced countermeasure evidence, and the nuclear and famine pathways in war_exceeds_10pct are unsourced.

Mechanically, each conditional switch excludes its prerequisite and the rule supplies it. The autonomy gate appears once in each route that uses it. The bio and war routes have no autonomy gate, which is intended. The central and endpoint values are judgment and are not independently measured.

Only the autonomy gate is shared. The war, bio and cyber routes are treated as independent given their prerequisites, though a great-power conflict could coincide with cyber collapse or raise attack incentives. The shared resilience factor is missing, so mortality conditionals may be correlated. The loss-of-control route supplies most of the rough total, so omitted correlations matter most where the war and cyber routes overlap.

The route-specific >10% switches are judgment values with no mortality model behind them. The threshold is about 0.8 billion deaths in the window. Reaching it through infrastructure outages, bio events or accidental failures requires extreme cascades, and the model does not represent timing of deaths within the window or the attribution requirement beyond the rationale text. The OWID source gives historical war deaths in absolute numbers, so it supports only a scale comparison.

No sensitivity output is re-read in this response, so I cannot restate computed swings from the harness. The largest sensitivity is judged to be the loss-of-control disempowerment and its mortality switch, both judgment-dominated. No parameter has been tuned to reach a preferred total, and the candidate is not recalibrated here.

Assumption scenarios, missing evidence and structural uncertainty are distinguished. Most parameters are judgment, no route has a measured rate, and structural uncertainty is large: the independent-route decomposition and collapsed window timing could move the result either way. The result is a judgment-based model output, not a calibrated forecast.
